narrator: Dr. Seward (phonograph diary), Mina Harker (journal), Jonathan Harker (journal)
summary: Van Helsing receives Mina's telegram at the Berkeley Hotel, hands Seward the Harker diaries and departs for Whitby. Seward meets Mina at Paddington and brings her to the asylum at Purfleet. Mina learns of the phonograph diary, wins Seward's trust by showing him her typescripts, and spends the night typing out the cylinders about Lucy's death in three manifold copies. Jonathan, back from Whitby and London, has traced the fifty earth boxes from the Demeter through Whitby, King's Cross and Carter Paterson to Carfax chapel. Seward realises the Count's lair is the house next door and that Renfield has been an index of the Count's presence; Renfield is suspiciously calm. Lord Godalming and Quincey Morris arrive and Mina consoles each in turn, forging a bond of 'sister' and 'little girl'.

scenes.title: Telegram at the Berkeley Hotel
scenes.summary: Van Helsing finds Mina's telegram, orders Seward to meet her, gives him typescripts of Jonathan's and Mina's diaries and leaves for Liverpool Street and Whitby.
scenes.key_quote: may be the beginning of the end to you and me and many another; or it may sound the knell of the Un-Dead who walk the earth.

scenes.title: Meeting at Paddington
scenes.location: Paddington station, then Underground to Fenchurch Street, then Purfleet asylum
scenes.summary: Mina recognises Seward from Lucy's description; they travel with her typewriter to the asylum, where she shudders on entering.
scenes.key_quote: I knew you from the description of poor dear Lucy; but——

scenes.title: The phonograph in the study
scenes.summary: Mina discovers the phonograph, asks to hear Lucy's death; Seward refuses in horror until she points to her own typescripts. He gives her the wax cylinders, the first half-dozen being personal.
scenes.key_quote: Tell you of her death? Not for the wide world!

scenes.title: Mina hears the cylinders
scenes.summary: Mina listens through the forked ear-tubes, is overcome by the story of Lucy's death and revived with brandy, then types all cylinders from the seventh in three manifold copies. She borrows newspaper files.
scenes.key_quote: In this matter dates are everything

scenes.title: Harker's trail of the boxes
scenes.location: Whitby, King's Cross, Carter Paterson's central office
scenes.summary: Jonathan inspects invoices, coastguards, station-masters and carriers; every tally confirms fifty cases of earth reached Carfax chapel. A carrier describes the house as the 'rummiest' he was ever in.
scenes.key_quote: Fifty cases of common earth, to be used for experimental purposes.

scenes.title: Seward reads the typescripts and visits Renfield
scenes.summary: Seward realises Carfax is next door. Renfield is unnaturally calm, speaks of discharge, and Seward orders the attendant to keep a strait-waistcoat ready.
scenes.key_quote: I mistrust these quiet moods of his

scenes.title: Mina comforts Godalming and Morris
scenes.summary: Mina gives both suitors of Lucy the typed record. Godalming weeps on her shoulder; Morris kisses her hand and calls her 'little girl'.
scenes.key_quote: Little girl, you will never regret that true-hearted kindness, so long as ever you live!

locations.name: Berkeley Hotel
locations.description: London hotel where Van Helsing stays; telegram waits there; later has a directory.
locations.quote: When we arrived at the Berkeley Hotel, Van Helsing found a telegram waiting for him

locations.name: Paddington station platform
locations.description: Arrival platform with crowd that melts away after the train.
locations.quote: The crowd melted away, after the bustling fashion common to arrival platforms

locations.name: Dr. Seward's study
locations.description: Study with a table holding the phonograph, a large drawer of wax cylinders, a cupboard with a case-bottle of brandy, and stacked typewriting.
locations.quote: He stood up and opened a large drawer, in which were arranged in order a number of hollow cylinders of metal covered with dark wax

locations.name: Purfleet asylum (Seward's house)
locations.description: Lunatic asylum with study, library, sitting-room and bedroom for Mrs. Harker, corridors, window overlooking the garden.
locations.quote: she was unable to repress a shudder when we entered.

locations.name: Renfield's room
locations.description: Cell where Renfield sits placidly with folded hands, smiling.
locations.quote: I found Renfield sitting placidly in his room with his hands folded, smiling benignly.

locations.name: Whitby harbour, station and Billington's office
locations.description: Port with coastguards, Customs, harbour-master and station where boxes were received.
locations.atmosphere: local legend of the strange ship
locations.quote: the strange entry of the ship, which is already taking its place in local tradition

locations.name: Carfax, old chapel and house (as described by carriers)
locations.description: A house untouched for a hundred years, dust thick enough to sleep on, smelling of old Jerusalem; the old chapel is the worst.
locations.quote: I wouldn’t take less nor a quid a moment to stay there arter dark.

characters.name: Dr. John Seward
characters.appearance: blushes, grows deathly pale when pressed
characters.personality: noble, shy, grief-stricken, honest; embarrassed to the point of boyishness
notable_lines: I gave myself away that time!

characters.name: Mina Harker
characters.appearance: sweet-faced, dainty-looking girl; red-eyed from weeping
notable_lines: Let me write this all out now. We must be ready for Dr. Van Helsing when he comes.

characters.name: Abraham Van Helsing
characters.personality: delighted by Mina, grave about the evidence
notable_lines: Ah, that wonderful Madam Mina, pearl among women!

characters.name: Jonathan Harker
characters.appearance: quiet business-like gentleman, full of energy
characters.speech_style: methodical, dry humour about the carriers' thirst

characters.name: Lord Godalming (Arthur Holmwood)
notable_lines: I have had one lesson already in accepting facts that should make a man humble to the last hour of his life.

characters.name: Quincey Morris
notable_lines: Little girl, you will never regret that true-hearted kindness, so long as ever you live!

characters.name: Carter Paterson carrier
notable_lines: That ’ere ’ouse, guv’nor, is the rummiest I ever was in.

objects.name: Telegram from Mina
objects.description: 'Am coming up by train. Jonathan at Whitby. Important news.—Mina Harker.'
objects.function_in_story: Summons Seward to the station, redirects Van Helsing to Whitby.
objects.quote: Am coming up by train. Jonathan at Whitby. Important news.—Mina Harker.

objects.name: Typewritten copy of Jonathan Harker's diary
objects.description: Typed manuscript of the Transylvania diary.
objects.quote: gave me a typewritten copy of it, as also of Mrs. Harker’s diary at Whitby

objects.name: Phonograph
objects.description: Seward's diary machine, with a forked metal ear-piece for listening, adjustable speed and a stop control.
objects.function_in_story: Stores Seward's diary on wax cylinders; Mina listens and types from it.
objects.quote: I put the forked metal to my ears and listened.

objects.name: Wax cylinders
objects.description: Hollow metal cylinders covered with dark wax stored in order in a large drawer.
objects.function_in_story: Holds the account of Lucy's death; first six are personal.
objects.quote: a number of hollow cylinders of metal covered with dark wax

objects.name: Typewriter
objects.description: Mina's portable typewriter; she uses manifold paper to make three copies.
objects.quote: I used manifold, and so took three copies of the diary

objects.name: Case-bottle of brandy
objects.description: Bottle kept in a cupboard in the study.
objects.function_in_story: Revives Mina after hearing the cylinders.
objects.quote: hurriedly taking a case-bottle from a cupboard, gave me some brandy

objects.name: Newspaper files
objects.description: Westminster Gazette and Pall Mall Gazette files kept by Seward; also Mina's cuttings from the Dailygraph and Whitby Gazette.
objects.function_in_story: Source of clues to the Count's movements.
objects.quote: I borrowed the files of “The Westminster Gazette” and “The Pall Mall Gazette,”

objects.name: Invoice: fifty cases of common earth
objects.quote: “Fifty cases of common earth, to be used for experimental purposes.”

objects.name: Carter Paterson way-bill and letters
objects.description: Day-book, letter-book and way-bill of the London carriers.
objects.function_in_story: Proves delivery of boxes to Carfax.
objects.quote: the way-bill and all the papers connected with the delivery of the boxes at Carfax

objects.name: Letters about the purchase of Carfax
objects.description: Bundle of letters filed with the typescript.
objects.function_in_story: Reveals the Count bought the house next door.
objects.quote: The bundle of letters relating to the purchase of the house were with the typescript.

objects.name: Strait-waistcoat
objects.quote: to have a strait-waistcoat ready in case of need

objects.name: Earth boxes (50)
objects.description: Fifty cases of earth, 'main and mortal heavy', stored in Carfax chapel.
objects.quote: the boxes were “main and mortal heavy,”

creatures.name: The Count (offstage)
creatures.description: Referred to as 'this Thing', not human, not beast.
creatures.behaviour: His lair is next to the asylum; Renfield's moods track his proximity.
creatures.quote: this Thing is not human—not even beast.

creatures.name: Renfield (zoophagous patient)
creatures.description: Eats flies and spiders; bound to the Count.
creatures.behaviour: Calm when the Count's triumph seems assured.

vampire_lore.rule: Renfield's moods are linked to the Count's proximity
vampire_lore.detail: All his outbreaks correlate with the Count's presence; calm may mean satisfied instinct.
vampire_lore.quote: All those outbreaks were in some way linked with the proximity of the Count.

vampire_lore.detail: He prepared for every obstacle and 'took no chances'.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire lair is disused, foul and dusty
vampire_lore.detail: Carfax untouched for a century, chapel smells terrible, men flee after dark.
vampire_lore.quote: the ole chapel—that took the cike, that did!

puzzles.name: Trace the boxes by paperwork
puzzles.setup: Fifty earth boxes landed at Whitby.
puzzles.obstacle: Need to confirm where they went.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker follows invoice, station-masters, carriers' tally and way-bill to Carfax; tips loosen tongues.
puzzles.game_idea: Investigation puzzle: match documents and testimony tallies; each tip unlocks a witness.
puzzles.quote: Here again I found the tally agreeing exactly

puzzles.name: Collate evidence chronologically
puzzles.book_solution: Mina types and orders the cylinders and diaries; dates reveal Renfield's outbursts match the Count's visits.
puzzles.game_idea: Timeline puzzle: sort document fragments onto a calendar to reveal a hidden pattern.
puzzles.quote: if we get all our material ready, and have every item put in chronological order, we shall have done much.

puzzles.name: Win Seward's trust
puzzles.setup: Seward refuses to share Lucy's death account.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina shows her own typed diaries.
puzzles.game_idea: Dialogue puzzle: choose proofs of trustworthiness.
puzzles.quote: You do not know me... When you have read those papers... you will know me better.

crafting.result: Three typed manifold copies of the diary
crafting.method: Play cylinders at slow pace and type from the beginning of the seventh.
crafting.purpose: Evidence set for the whole party
crafting.quote: He accordingly set the phonograph at a slow pace, and I began to typewrite from the beginning of the seventh cylinder.

Gain Seward's trust to obtain the cylinders.
Collate the evidence into a timeline to reveal Renfield's link to the Count.
Follow the delivery trail of the fifty boxes from Whitby to Carfax.
